title: Ed Yardeni's Economic Reality Check: It's Not a Crisis
speaker: Ed Yardeni

macro_themes.view: US yield rise reflects a stronger economy and higher neutral rate ('normal for longer'), not a sovereign debt crisis.
France is in a genuine debt crisis; Japan's carry-trade unwind is pushing yields up globally in sync.
S&P 500 near record on strong earnings, though equal-weight is ~6% off its August peak.
Current inflation not a 5-10 year problem; productivity will bring it down.
Bessent's tools so far a peashooter; would need a bigger buyback 'bazooka' in a disorderly unwind.

calls.reason: Yields could still go higher near term (bond vigilantes), so dollar-cost average; over 5-10 years inflation falls on productivity, making current yields attractive (bullish bonds = bearish yields).
calls.quote: there still is a potential for this thing to go higher again... from a 5year 10-year basis... these are pretty good yields.

notes: No date spoken ('this morning we put out a research piece', Bessent 'over the weekend'); listing date. 10y quoted ~5.2-5.3 by host, no precise level, price_at_call null.
